title: Papilledema: Optic Disc Findings and Clinical Context
subject: Ophthalmology
preview: Papilledema is optic disc swelling associated with raised intracranial pressure, but disc swelling has other causes.
quickRevision: Papilledema is optic disc swelling associated with raised intracranial pressure, but disc swelling has other causes.
Assess headache, neurologic signs, vision and intracranial causes before procedures such as lumbar puncture.
Optic disc appearance is not interchangeable with visual function; acuity can be preserved early.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: Papilledema is optic disc swelling associated with raised intracranial pressure, but disc swelling has other causes.
Blurred disc margins, vessel obscuration and hemorrhages can be clues on fundus examination.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: Assess headache, neurologic signs, vision and intracranial causes before procedures such as lumbar puncture.
Optic disc appearance is not interchangeable with visual function; acuity can be preserved early.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Not every swollen optic disc is papilledema, and a normal fundus does not exclude early raised intracranial pressure.

quiz.question: What does papilledema specifically imply?
options: Optic disc swelling due to raised intracranial pressure
